about.title: Carmel Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Carmel's mix of boutique storefronts, hillside walkways, and older sidewalks along Ocean Avenue and Junipero Avenue creates plenty of opportunities for uneven surfaces, poor lighting, and slick tile to go unaddressed. When a property owner or business fails to fix a known hazard, or doesn't warn visitors about it, people get hurt. Under California law, you generally need to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and didn't act. That's why documenting the scene, taking photos, and requesting surveillance footage early matters so much. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result. What we do is connect you, free of charge, with an independent local attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather evidence before it disappears, and walk you through your options under a contingency arrangement, meaning there's no fee unless your case recovers something.

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California premises cases hinge on proving the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney in our network knows how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Time-Sensitive Evidence Gets Protected
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a Carmel shop or restaurant often gets overwritten within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that reflects the full picture, not just what a property owner claims.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Carmel?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim, sometimes within months. It's worth having an attorney review the timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the store or business says I was careless?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility, though the amount may be reduced accordingly. An independent attorney can help gather evidence, like footage from Ocean Avenue storefronts or San Carlos Street businesses, to show what really contributed to the fall.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we never charge you to find an independent attorney. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your claim results in a recovery.
